name: Camargue
blurb: Brine lagoons, pink flamingos and wild horses in the Rhone delta.

tip.title: Freshen the lagoons
tip.text: Brine shrimp thrive where the water is very salty because fish stay out. Set Salt and brine to -100% and watch the shrimp, then the flamingos that filter them.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong Mediterranean sun drives algal growth in shallow lagoons and evaporates water from the salt pans, concentrating the brine.

nodes.name: Rhone water and silt
nodes.desc: The Rhone splits into two arms that feed the delta with fresh water and mud. Some of the lagoons are remnants of old river channels.

nodes.name: Salt and brine
nodes.desc: Lagoons cut off from the sea by sandbars and long-used salt pans hold salty water. Brine shrimp tolerate salinity that keeps most fish out.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead reed, marsh plants, dung and carcasses, returning nutrients to the delta mud.

nodes.name: Lagoon microalgae
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae, including salt-loving types, grow in sunlit lagoons. Brine shrimp feed on planktonic algae; flamingos also take diatoms and blue-green algae.

nodes.name: Common reed
nodes.desc: Dominant plant of the freshwater reedbeds that ring the lagoons. It gives nesting cover for marsh harriers and food for coypu and coots.

nodes.name: Sea rush and salt meadow
nodes.desc: Rushes and salt-tolerant grasses of the brackish meadows where semi-wild horses and cattle graze.

nodes.name: Glasswort
nodes.desc: A succulent salt-tolerant shrub of the saline flats, recorded commonly around the lagoons; one of the plants adapted to the salty conditions.

nodes.name: Brine shrimp
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans of salt lakes and brine ponds. Their tolerance of very salty water helps them escape most fish predators.

nodes.name: Midge larvae
nodes.desc: Aquatic insect larvae in lagoon mud and shallows. Flamingos and ibises list insect larvae such as chironomids among their food.

nodes.name: Camargue horse
nodes.desc: A hardy white horse that lives semi-wild in the Rhone delta marshes. Its wide hooves suit the soggy ground, and gardians ride it to herd cattle.

nodes.name: Camargue cattle
nodes.desc: Dark, semi-wild cattle that roam the marshes under the care of gardians and supply the bulls for the local bull-running tradition.

nodes.name: Coypu
nodes.desc: A South American rodent living in the marshes; GloBI records it eating common reed.

nodes.name: Eurasian coot
nodes.desc: A common waterbird of lagoons and reedbeds; GloBI records it eating common reed and other plants.

nodes.name: Greater flamingo
nodes.desc: Filters brine shrimp, algae, insect larvae and molluscs from shallow saline water. Yellow-legged gulls take many of its eggs and chicks around the Mediterranean.

nodes.name: Glossy ibis
nodes.desc: Wades in very shallow water for insect larvae, worms, snails and crustaceans, plus the occasional frog.

nodes.name: Marsh frog
nodes.desc: A large water frog of ponds and channels that eats insects; it is prey for herons, ibises, harriers and foxes in GloBI records.

nodes.name: European eel
nodes.desc: Eats worms, fish, molluscs and crustaceans. Critically endangered, with numbers reaching Europe down by about 90% since the 1970s.

nodes.name: Grey heron
nodes.desc: Wading predator of frogs, small mammals, coots and fish; GloBI also records it taking coypu. The European eel page lists herons as eel predators.

nodes.name: Yellow-legged gull
nodes.desc: Opportunistic gull that scavenges. Around the Mediterranean it accounts for about half of the predation on flamingo eggs and chicks.

nodes.name: Western marsh harrier
nodes.desc: Nests in reedbeds and hunts low over the marsh for birds, small mammals and frogs. GloBI records flamingo, ibis, coot and marsh frog among its prey.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist predator and scavenger of the marsh edges. GloBI records it eating coypu, coots, flamingos, gulls and marsh frogs.
